exposure: antenatal corticosteroid treatment (ACT) timing (no ACT, ACT < 34 weeks' gestation, ACT ≥ 34 weeks' gestation)
outcome: neonatal intensive care unit admission rate
cohort: The study included women with dichorionic-diamniotic twin pregnancies who experienced a late preterm birth between 2017 and 2021 at a large referral hospital.
finding: Antenatal corticosteroid treatment (ACT) at or after 34 weeks' gestation was not associated with improved composite respiratory or neonatal outcomes, but it was associated with a higher rate of neonatal hypoglycemia compared to no ACT.
birth_weight: N/A (birthweight was measured and associated with outcomes, but no specific range for inclusion was given)
gest_age: late preterm (defined as 34 0/7 weeks to 36 6/7 weeks)
